title: Redundant Trivial Getter Comment
pattern: Doc-comment on a trivial getter function that simply restates the function name.
why_bad: Dual-maintenance hazard and visual noise. Renaming the method requires updating the doc-comment, with zero added semantic value for the reader.
detection: Doc-comment on a function returning a field of the same name, where the comment's text merely converts the name's snake_case to standard English words.
counterexample: A getter doc-comment adding real contract information beyond the name, such as units, valid ranges, stability guarantees, or caching behavior.
source: Kent Beck, *Tidy First?* (2023), Chapter 15 ("Delete Redundant Comments"); John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 13.2 ("Red Flag: Comment Repeats Code").
